author: GamingBolt
description:
Phantom Blade Zero is out now and a pretty strong success by both reported and legitimate accounts (if Steam concurrent player counts are anything to go by). Set in a distinct kungfupunk universe and telling a Wuxia that's much closer to dark fantasy, the story focuses on Soul, a former Order assassin now on the run after killing its leader. He also has 66 days to live, which is just the icing on top of this disaster sundae.

However, it's also the latest hack-and-slash action RPG to be developed on Unreal Engine 5, following in the footsteps of smash hit Black Myth: Wukong, free-to-play title Where Winds Meet, and upcoming titles like Nodusfall, Tides of Annihilation, etc.

Granted, it's permeated the industry on a much wider scale, but thus far, its track record in this genre has proven solid. The question now is how Phantom Blade Zero performs on PS5 and PC.
title: Phantom Blade Zero PS5 vs PC Graphics Comparison - A Stunning Tech Showcase?

author: GamingBolt
description:
“Take a break and come back” became one of my favorite phrases while playing Hollow Knight: Silksong last year. It can sound patronising initially because why would you want to stop playing? You're having fun, right? However, it's surprisingly effective at getting past a frustrating boss or coming back to a challenge completely refreshed.

What does that have to do with Phantom Blade Zero, S-Game's hack-and-slash action RPG, which is already one of 2026's highest-rated games, especially amid so much stiff competition? The same game that's dominating the global top sellers chart on Steam? Well, for much of my time playing, only one sentiment truly ruled – one thought that dominated everything else.

I don't want to stop.
title: Why I Can't STOP Playing Phantom Blade Zero

description:

Check out ATMOSFAR: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1798230/ATMOSFAR/

It's been a busy season for survival crafting games, with several reaching 1.0 – the culmination of years of development, feedback and updates. However, all ends are beginnings, and that means a fresh crop of new titles to look forward to in the genre. One such effort is Atmosfar, entering Steam Early Access on October 29th for $24.99, and offering a more exploration-heavy, atmospheric (no pun intended) experience.

Developed by Apog Labs and published by Shueisha Games, who also sponsored this video, Atmosfar offers co-op for up to four players, but it's also perfectly enjoyable solo. Having gone hands-on with early access and even completed the story content on offer, here are 15 things you should know.
title: 400,000 Players Want This Game - ATMOSFAR: 15 Things You Need To Know
